hero_copy.headline: 84% of Ahmedabad's water comes down one canal
hero_copy.body: Ahmedabad draws 1,850 MLD a day. 1,550 of it comes from three offtakes on the Narmada Main Canal, which carries water from Sardar Sarovar dam; 200 MLD comes from the Mahi through the Shedhi branch canal, and 100 MLD from 555 borewells. The Sabarmati, the river {city} was founded on, supplies none of it, and the water held in the river through the riverfront is topped up from the same Narmada canal. AMC's 2023-24 budget said the tap runs two hours a day, from 6 to 8 in the morning, through unmetered connections.
hero_copy.wtp_sub: 1,750 MLD at Kotarpur (1,150), Jaspur (400) and Raska (200); 1,700 MLD treated a day. Work under way or planned would take it to 2,700.
hero_copy.footer: Figures from AMC Budget 2026-27, pp.63-64 (Gujarati, February 2026). AMC publishes no measured non-revenue water and no entitlement from the Narmada; both are named gaps on the About page.

supply_chain: Sardar Sarovar dam on the Narmada
Narmada Main Canal: head regulators 1 and 2 to Kotarpur, the Dholka branch to Jaspur
Kadana dam and the Wanakbori weir on the Mahi, through the Shedhi branch canal to Raska
Three treatment plants, 1,750 MLD; 240 distribution stations
5,575 km of supply lines and 555 km of trunk mains

current_supply_mix_mld.scheme: Pumped into distribution stations and isolated networks
current_supply_mix_mld.note: 315 MLD capacity, 100 used. The table's own sub-count (322 isolated + 238 station-connected) sums to 560, not 555.

_supply_total_note: Source-side use. AMC's treatment-side figure for the same day is 1,700 MLD; the two are different measures in one table.

distribution.note: Population left out: the same budget says about 90 lakh on p.63 and 80 lakh on p.9.

groundwater._note: AMC's own borewell draw. Private borewells are not in any AMC figure. For the aquifer under the city, see the groundwater page: IN-GRES assesses the Ahmedabad Urban unit as over-exploited.
